# REST API: Principals

These routes of the platform API come from its [OpenAPI document](../openapi.json); [The REST API as a contract](../rest-api.md) says what Lakana promises about them.

## `POST /api/v1/principals`

Create a principal

From the web interface it needs a passkey touch within the last 15 minutes (403 `StepUpRequired`); a token never does.

Answers 409 when an access file manages the scope; `override_managed` with `override_reason` overrides it (ADMIN on the instance; audited). Only a service account is managed by a file: for a person the override answers 422.

Creates a user or a service account. Needs `MANAGE_PRINCIPAL` on the instance. Answers 409 when the name is taken.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `override_managed` | query | no | true or false | Change access in a scope an access file manages anyway, in an emergency. Needs the ADMIN role on the instance and `override_reason`; audited, and shown as drift until the next apply. |
| `override_reason` | query | no | text or null | Why, 10 to 500 characters on one line; with `override_managed=true`. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Request body (application/json, required): `PrincipalCreate`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | yes |  |
| `type` | one of `USER`, `SERVICE_ACCOUNT` | yes |  |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `201` | Successful Response | `PrincipalOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `PrincipalOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | yes |  |
| `type` | text | yes |  |
| `is_active` | true or false | yes |  |
| `picture` | text or null | no |  |
| `held_admin` | true or false or null | no |  |

## `GET /api/v1/principals`

List principals

Lists the principals, newest first. Needs `MANAGE_PRINCIPAL` on the instance. The cursor of the next page is in the `X-Next-Cursor` response header and is absent on the last page.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `q` | query | no | text or null | Only principals whose name contains this text, in any letter case. |
| `limit` | query | no | whole number | Most principals returned (1 to 200). |
| `cursor` | query | no | text or null | The `X-Next-Cursor` of the previous page; send the same `q`. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | list of `PrincipalOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

## `DELETE /api/v1/principals/{name}`

Deactivate a principal

Stops the principal from signing in. The record stays, with every grant, token and audit entry that refers to it. Needs `MANAGE_PRINCIPAL` on the instance. Answers 404 when there is no principal of that name and 409 when it is the last active administrator.

Answers 409 when an access file manages the scope; `override_managed` with `override_reason` overrides it (ADMIN on the instance; audited). Only a service account is managed by a file: for a person the override answers 422.

From the web interface it needs a passkey touch within the last 15 minutes (403 `StepUpRequired`); a token never does.

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |

| `override_managed` | query | no | true or false | Change access in a scope an access file manages anyway, in an emergency. Needs the ADMIN role on the instance and `override_reason`; audited, and shown as drift until the next apply. |
| `override_reason` | query | no | text or null | Why, 10 to 500 characters on one line; with `override_managed=true`. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `204` | Successful Response | none |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |

## `GET /api/v1/principals/{name}/permissions`

Explain what a principal may do

Says, action by action, what the principal may do on an object and through which grant. The object is named like the filter of the grants list; none names the instance. A caller may ask about itself; about anyone else it needs the `ADMIN` role on the instance. Answers 404 to an administrator for a principal or object that does not exist, and 422 when the object is named incompletely.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | path | yes | text | The principal asked about. |
| `environment` | query | no | text or null | The object's environment. |
| `namespace` | query | no | text or null | The object's dot-joined namespace. |
| `table` | query | no | text or null | The object's table. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `PermissionsOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `PermissionsOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `principal` | text | yes |  |
| `active` | true or false | yes |  |
| `scope` | `ScopeOut` | yes |  |
| `permissions` | list of `PermissionOut` | yes |  |
| `note` | text or null | yes |  |

## `GET /api/v1/principals/{name}/grants`

List the grants a principal holds

The live grants naming the principal and those of every group it belongs to now, newest first, each with the group's name (`null` for a direct grant). A caller may ask about itself with a session or a personal token, with no right at all; about anyone else it needs the `ADMIN` role on the instance, and a task or CI token may not ask even about its own principal. The refusal comes before any lookup, so it never says whether the principal exists; an administrator gets 404 for one that does not. It carries nothing about other people: no `granted_by`, no principal id.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | path | yes | text | The principal asked about. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | list of `HeldGrantOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

## `GET /api/v1/principals/{name}/sessions`

List a person's open browser sessions

Anyone may list their own; listing another person's needs the ADMIN role on the instance (403 otherwise). The session the request came with is marked `current`. A session past its idle timeout or lifetime is not listed.

## `DELETE /api/v1/principals/{name}/sessions`

End all of a person's browser sessions

Your own: sign out everywhere, including this browser. Another person's: needs the ADMIN role on the instance and, from the web interface, a passkey touch within the last 15 minutes (403 `StepUpRequired` otherwise); each ended session is recorded in the audit log with your name.

| `204` | Successful Response | none |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |

## `POST /api/v1/principals/{name}/passkeys`

Finish adding a passkey to your own account

Send the browser's `credential.toJSON()` for the ceremony the options route started, and optionally a name for the passkey. An answer from another address or without user verification, or a used or expired challenge, answers 403 `PasskeyRefused`; a passkey that is registered already answers 409. Adding a passkey counts as a passkey touch.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | path | yes | text | Your own principal name. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Request body (application/json, required): `PasskeyRegisterIn`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ceremony_id` | text (uuid) | yes |  |
| `credential` | mapping of text to any | yes |  |
| `name` | text or null | no |  |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `201` | Successful Response | `PasskeyOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `PasskeyOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | text (uuid) | yes |  |
| `name` | text | yes |  |
| `created_at` | text (date-time) | yes |  |
| `last_used_at` | text (date-time) or null | yes |  |
| `backup_eligible` | true or false | yes |  |
| `disabled_reason` | text or null | yes |  |
| `usable_here` | true or false | yes |  |

## `POST /api/v1/principals/{name}/passkeys/options`

Start adding a passkey to your own account

From the web interface only (a token gets 409). The first passkey may be added within 15 minutes of signing in with a setup, invite or recovery link; every later one needs a passkey touch within the last 15 minutes (403 `StepUpRequired`). A session from a local sign-in link may add only the first passkey. After those 15 minutes, a session from a link or a local sign-in without a usable passkey gets a 403 that names `lakana server start --local` or a recovery link, since a touch cannot help it. A person linked to the identity provider signs in only there and gets 403 `ProviderSignInRequired`. The options ask for a discoverable passkey with user verification (a PIN, fingerprint or face) and no attestation.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | path | yes | text | Your own principal name. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `PasskeyOptionsOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `PasskeyOptionsOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ceremony_id` | text (uuid) | yes |  |
| `public_key` | mapping of text to any | yes |  |

## `DELETE /api/v1/principals/{name}/passkeys/{passkey_id}`

Remove a passkey

Your own, or, with the ADMIN role on the instance, anyone's. From the web interface it needs a passkey touch within the last 15 minutes (403 `StepUpRequired`). Your own last working passkey cannot be removed (409): add another one first, or ask an administrator for a recovery link. An administrator removing another person's passkey also ends all of that person's browser sessions.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | path | yes | text | The person's principal name. |
| `passkey_id` | path | yes | text (uuid) | The passkey's id, from the list. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `204` | Successful Response | none |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

## `PUT /api/v1/principals/{name}/picture`

Set your profile picture

Send the image file as the body, with its type as `Content-Type`: `image/jpeg`, `image/png` or `image/webp` (415 for any other, SVG included). At most 5 MB (413) and 40 megapixels (422). The server keeps a new 256 x 256 picture cut from the centre and turned upright, with none of the file's metadata (location, camera); 422 when the file is not a readable image of the type sent. Only your own (403 for another name, and for a task or CI token). One upload of yours at a time, and a few in all per server: otherwise 503, try again after `Retry-After`. Audited.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | path | yes | text | Your principal name. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `PictureOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `400` | The client closed the connection before the request body arrived in full. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `408` | No part of the request body arrived within the read timeout. | `ErrorOut` |
| `413` | The request body is larger than the server accepts. | `ErrorOut` |
| `415` | The request body is of a type the server does not accept; the message names the ones it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `503` | The server cannot do this right now; ask again after the time in `Retry-After`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `PictureOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `etag` | text | yes |  |

## `GET /api/v1/principals/{name}/picture`

Show a person's profile picture

Your own always; anyone's once you have access (any grant, or the `ADMIN` role); 403 for a person without access yet, and for a task or CI token. 404 when the person has no picture. The answer carries an `ETag` (the `picture` field of the principal and of whoami) and is cached privately for a day; send `If-None-Match` for a 304.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | path | yes | text | The person's principal name. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | The picture, a 256 x 256 WebP. | `image/webp` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `304` | The picture is still the one `If-None-Match` names. | none |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |
